tagline: From Jacob Lake to the North Rim, through pine and aspen.
intro: From Jacob Lake, at about 8,000 feet in a ponderosa pine forest, State Route 67 runs south across the Kaibab Plateau to the North Rim of the Grand Canyon, the sole road linking the two. The way lies through mixed conifer forest with fir and quaking aspen, past sub-alpine meadows, ponds and limestone outcrops. The Forest Service passes along someone's verdict that these are the most pleasant 44 miles in America.
The road was built in the late 1920s, as the North Rim was getting its first lodge and ranger residence. The plateau rises to 9,200 feet, and its winter snowfall sometimes passes 17 feet.

moments.title: Jacob Lake Lookout Tower
moments.text: The Civilian Conservation Corps put up this 80-foot steel tower in 1934, and visitors may still climb it to the cab and its Osborne Fire Finder.

moments.title: Kaibab meadows
moments.text: North of the park entrance the road runs down a narrow meadow bordered by evergreens, in the cool forest that is the only home of the Kaibab squirrel.

moments.title: Bright Angel Point
moments.text: A paved trail of three-quarters of a mile follows the ridge out to the point, with a campground 4,000 feet below and Grand Canyon Village about 10 miles off across the canyon.

practical: Heavy snow normally closes SR 67 from November through mid-May, and services along the route are limited. The main building of the Grand Canyon Lodge at the North Rim burned in the Dragon Bravo Fire of July 2025.
